title: From learning theory to trustworthy AI in the physical world.
intro: Our research connects four areas: learning theory, data governance, model and agent security, and safe embodied intelligence.

directions.title: Learning Theory: Trustworthy AI Foundations
directions.question: What makes learning reliable under adversarial data, supervision, and evaluation?
directions.description: Core algorithms and theory for trustworthy machine learning, from adversarial training and robust generalisation to representation alignment.
directions.pageIntro: We study why adversarially trained models succeed on some examples and fail on others. Our work spans generalisation, representation learning, and training methods that account for the geometry and distribution of the data.

focus.title: Robust generalisation
focus.detail: Examine when adversarial training generalises, including the accuracy–robustness trade-off and the role of sample geometry.

focus.title: Reliable representations
focus.detail: Analyse how individual training examples affect contrastive representations and where misalignment arises.

focus.title: Robust training methods
focus.detail: Use distributional discrepancy, pixel reweighting, and coreset selection to improve or simplify robust training.

papers.title: Benign Overfitting in Adversarial Training for Vision Transformers
papers.label: Robust generalisation
papers.summary: Studies benign overfitting and generalisation in adversarially trained vision transformers.

papers.title: Dissecting Representation Misalignment in Contrastive Learning via Influence Function
papers.label: Representation analysis
papers.summary: Uses influence-function analysis to examine representation misalignment in contrastive learning.

papers.title: One Stone, Two Birds: Enhancing Adversarial Defense Through the Lens of Distributional Discrepancy
papers.label: Distributional robustness
papers.summary: Approaches adversarial defence through the distributional discrepancy between clean and adversarial data.

papers.title: Improving Accuracy-Robustness Trade-off via Pixel Reweighted Adversarial Training
papers.label: Adversarial training
papers.summary: Studies the accuracy–robustness trade-off through pixel-reweighted adversarial training.

papers.title: Efficient Adversarial Contrastive Learning via Robustness-Aware Coreset Selection
papers.label: Efficient robust learning
papers.summary: Makes adversarial contrastive learning more efficient with robustness-aware coreset selection.

papers.title: Geometry-aware Instance-reweighted Adversarial Training
papers.label: Geometric learning theory
papers.summary: Uses instance geometry to reweight adversarial training; selected for an ICLR Oral.

talks.title: Attack and Defense Mechanisms in Trustworthy Machine Learning: Challenges and Future Directions
Robust Machine Learning in Adversarial Environments
Adversarial Robustness: From Basic Science to Applications

directions.title: AI Governance: Data Safety & Content Integrity
directions.question: How do we keep data-driven systems reliable when data can be poisoned, biased, noisy, or private?
directions.description: Security and governance at the data layer: poisoning and backdoors, algorithmic bias, privacy leakage, and defensible data use.
directions.pageIntro: Training data shape a model long before it reaches users. We investigate poisoning, bias, and privacy leakage in multimodal and generative systems, and develop ways to evaluate and reduce these risks.

focus.title: Poisoning & backdoors
focus.detail: Test how manipulated training examples affect multimodal models and downstream foundation-model tasks.

focus.title: Bias & fair generation
focus.detail: Examine fairness in text-to-image generation and methods for reducing disparities in generated outputs.

focus.title: Privacy-preserving adaptation
focus.detail: Study membership-inference and model-inversion risks in model adaptation and federated learning.

papers.title: MP-Nav: Enhancing Data Poisoning Attacks against Multimodal Learning
papers.label: Multimodal poisoning
papers.summary: Investigates data-poisoning attacks against multimodal learning systems.

papers.title: Fair Text-to-Image Diffusion via Fair Mapping
papers.label: Algorithmic fairness
papers.summary: Introduces fair mapping as a route to more equitable text-to-image diffusion.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Low-Rank Adaptation Against Membership Inference Attacks for Latent Diffusion Models
papers.label: Privacy protection
papers.summary: Protects low-rank adaptation of latent diffusion models against membership-inference attacks.

papers.title: Learning a Robust Foundation Model Against Clean-Label Data Poisoning Attacks at Downstream Tasks
papers.label: Clean-label poisoning
papers.summary: Studies foundation-model robustness to clean-label poisoning in downstream tasks.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Federated Learning
papers.label: Federated privacy
papers.summary: Addresses privacy in heterogeneous federated learning.

papers.title: Bilateral Dependency Optimization: Defending Against Model-Inversion Attacks
papers.label: Model inversion
papers.summary: Defends against model-inversion attacks through bilateral dependency optimisation.

talks.title: Privacy-Preserving Adaptation against Membership Inference Attacks for Latent Diffusion Models
Evaluating and Enhancing the Reliability of Semi-Supervised Learning

directions.title: Model Security: Local LLMs & Trustworthy Agents
directions.question: How can locally deployed models and agents be evaluated, aligned, and controlled before they act?
directions.description: Safety for LLMs and agentic systems, spanning local and private deployment, jailbreak robustness, alignment, and repeatable evaluation harnesses.
directions.pageIntro: Our published work examines jailbreaks, adversarial preferences, noisy feedback, and robust agent representations. We are bringing those findings into repeatable evaluations for language models and agents, including systems deployed locally.

focus.title: Local & private deployment
focus.detail: Study model adaptation and evaluation choices for settings where data or models need to remain under local control.

focus.title: Robust alignment
focus.detail: Test how prompt attacks, adversarial preferences, and noisy feedback affect model behaviour.

focus.title: Agent evaluation harnesses
focus.detail: Develop repeatable checks for agent behaviour before systems with tools or memory are put into use.

papers.title: AutoRAS: Learning Robust Agentic Systems with Primitive Representations
papers.label: Robust agents
papers.summary: Develops robust agentic systems around primitive representations.

papers.title: Safety at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey of Large Model and Agent Safety
papers.label: Safety landscape
papers.summary: Organises the threat models, methods, and open questions across large-model and agent safety.

papers.title: Short-length Adversarial Training Helps LLMs Defend Long-length Jailbreak Attacks: Theoretical and Empirical Evidence
papers.label: Jailbreak robustness
papers.summary: Provides theoretical and empirical evidence on adversarial training for long-length jailbreak defence.

papers.title: Adversarial Preference Learning for Robust LLM Alignment
papers.label: Robust alignment
papers.summary: Uses adversarial preference learning to strengthen LLM alignment.

papers.title: An LLM Can Fool Itself: A Prompt-Based Adversarial Attack
papers.label: Prompt attacks
papers.summary: Demonstrates a prompt-based adversarial attack in which an LLM can be induced to fool itself.

papers.title: Perplexity-aware Correction for Robust Alignment with Noisy Preferences
papers.label: Preference reliability
papers.summary: Uses perplexity-aware correction to improve alignment when preference data are noisy.

directions.title: Embodied Intelligence: Trustworthy Multimodal Robotics
directions.question: How can intelligent agents remain safe when perception becomes physical action?
directions.description: Trust mechanisms for vision-language-action models and embodied agents, including inference-time safeguards, adversarial testing, and physical-world backdoors.
directions.pageIntro: Embodied systems turn model outputs into physical actions. Our current work studies safety checks for vision-language-action models, adversarial inputs, and backdoor attacks carried by physical objects.

focus.title: Inference-time safeguards
focus.detail: Investigate concept-based checks that can be applied while a vision-language-action model is making a decision.

focus.title: Adversarial VLA evaluation
focus.detail: Test attacks and defences that transfer across different vision-language-action models.

focus.title: Physical-world threat models
focus.detail: Examine whether physical objects can act as backdoor triggers for goal-directed robot behaviour.

papers.title: Concept-Based Dictionary Learning for Inference-Time Safety in Vision Language Action Models
papers.label: Inference-time VLA safety
papers.summary: Uses concept-based dictionary learning to support inference-time safety in vision-language-action models.

papers.title: Model-agnostic Adversarial Attack and Defense for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.label: VLA attack & defence
papers.summary: Studies model-agnostic adversarial attacks and defences for vision-language-action systems.

papers.title: Goal-oriented Backdoor Attack against Vision-Language-Action Models via Physical Objects
papers.label: Physical backdoors
papers.summary: Examines goal-oriented backdoor attacks on vision-language-action models through physical objects.
